lines: // so the socket boxes, wall lines and clear zones stay untouched. North = z 5 (fascia), south = z 32 (mirror of 5).
import { fasciaBoard, pierPanel, awning, hangSign } from "../vocab.mjs";
-// the palette lists four banner dyes (white, black, brown, orange) and wall hanging signs, not every dye or wall sign the
-// vocabulary writes: a banner in a dye off the list takes the nearest listed one, a wall sign becomes the hanging sign of its wood
+// the palette lists four standing banners (white, black, brown, orange) and wall hanging signs, not the wall banners or every
+// dye the vocabulary writes: a wall banner becomes the standing banner of its dye, turned to face the same way (standing
+// rotation 0 faces south, 4 west, 8 north, 12 east), a banner in a dye off the list takes the nearest listed one, and a
+// wall sign becomes the hanging sign of its wood
const BANNER_DYE = { light_gray: "white", red: "brown" };
+const STANDING_ROTATION = { south: "0", west: "4", north: "8", east: "12" };
const withNbt = (nbt, key, value) => nbt && { ...nbt, value: { ...nbt.value, [key]: value } };
const sign = /^((?:minecraft:)?)(\w+)_wall_sign$/.exec(block);
if (sign) return { block: `${sign[1]}${sign[2]}_wall_hanging_sign`, state, nbt: withNbt(nbt, "id", { type: "string", value: "minecraft:hanging_sign" }) };
const banner = /^((?:minecraft:)?)(\w+)_wall_banner$/.exec(block);
-  if (!banner || !BANNER_DYE[banner[2]]) return { block, state, nbt };
-  const old = banner[2], dye = BANNER_DYE[old], pats = nbt?.value?.patterns;
+  if (!banner) return { block, state, nbt };
+  const old = banner[2], dye = BANNER_DYE[old] ?? old, pats = nbt?.value?.patterns;
+  const standing = { rotation: STANDING_ROTATION[state.facing] };
+  if (dye === old) return { block: `${banner[1]}${dye}_banner`, state: standing, nbt };
const contrast = dye === "white" ? "black" : "white";
// the cloth's own colour (the border) moves to the new cloth; a letter that now shares the cloth's dye would vanish, so it takes the contrast
const fixed = (pats?.value?.value ?? []).map((p) => {
if (p.color.value === dye) return { ...p, color: { type: "string", value: contrast } };
return p;
-  return { block: `${banner[1]}${dye}_wall_banner`, state, nbt: pats ? withNbt(nbt, "patterns", { ...pats, value: { ...pats.value, value: fixed } }) : nbt };
+  return { block: `${banner[1]}${dye}_banner`, state: standing, nbt: pats ? withNbt(nbt, "patterns", { ...pats, value: { ...pats.value, value: fixed } }) : nbt };
// the grid as the street sees it: every write goes through paletteBlock first

input.summary:
Shopfronts fixed in parts/shops.mjs: wall banners now map to the palette's standing banners of their dye (rotation 8/0/4/12 from facing), so the OFF-PALETTE line is gone. ./make.sh builds build.nbt; Shopfronts reports 368 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette, and mcd check finds no floating or unsupported banners.
The Cart passage REFUSED line (12 barrel writes over birch and dark oak planks) is from room 10, not this part, and is still open.
Banner letters are re-rotated, not re-rendered, so how they read from the street is unchecked.
left: Room 10 (Cart passage) refuses 12 barrel writes at x35..36 z13,14,23,24 y5 because the Grounds woodpiles already occupy those cells; that part is not mine, so it needs a fix in room-10 or the grounds part.

The banner letters are now standing banners at the same cells, with rotation from facing. mcd check finds them supported, but I have not rendered the fascia to confirm the letters read correctly from the street.
mcd check reports 22 orphans (smooth_stone_slab on the pavement and dark_oak_planks and stripped wood on the eaves). None are shopfront blocks, so they are outside this part.

waste.what: Worked out by hand which banner id maps to which palette entry and what each banner's rotation should be from its facing (north 8, south 0, west 4, east 12), by reading vocab helpers, brush-sign.mjs and the build library's B.banner.
waste.cost: about 6 shell reads and greps, one edit, two make.sh runs
waste.tool: A palette-aware helper, such as `mcd palette-map <wall_banner->standing>` or a runParts option that maps off-palette ids to their nearest palette block (wall banner -> standing banner with rotation from facing, wall sign -> hanging sign), would have made this one line of config.

waste.what: Checked by hand which banner cells had solid support below them, to know whether a standing banner would float.
waste.cost: about 3 reads of awning and plaque geometry
waste.tool: `mcd check --json` already reports unsupported standing banners; running it as a per-part gate in runParts (after each part, listing that part's floating cells) would have answered this without reading the geometry.

waste.what: Found the fix location by tracing plaque -> brush-sign bannerLetter -> wall banner writes, to see whether the banners came from the fascia or from bunting.
waste.tool: The make.sh OFF-PALETTE report could name the vocabulary helper and the call site (fasciaBoard -> plaque style banner) that emitted each off-palette id, so the source is shown directly.

companions.task: Check that the fascia letters (BIRCH, SPRUCE, OAK, JUNGLE, ACACIA, DK OAK) still read from the street now that they are standing banners at the same cells with rotation set from the facing, and that the dye swap kept the letter contrast.
